title: A prompt you keep, not retype
goal: See a reusable prompt as a recipe you write once and reuse — not a fresh instruction every time.

blocks.title: Stop retyping the same thing
blocks.body:
Every Monday you open a blank chat and type the same six lines: "You are a quiz-maker for Class 8 Science, make 5 MCQs, one mark each, add an answer key, keep the language simple…" Then you do it again on Thursday. And next week.

What if you wrote those instructions once — and just dropped in this week's topic? That's a mini-assistant. Four minutes here, and you'll never retype it again.

blocks.title: A saved recipe for a repeat job
blocks.body:
A reusable prompt is a recipe for a task you do again and again. You bake in the parts that never change, and leave a slot for the one part that does.

Three parts stay fixed:
• Role — who the AI is being ("You are a quiz-maker for my class").
• Context — your class, board, level ("Class 8 CBSE Science, mixed ability").
• Rules — what it must always do ("5 questions, one answer key, simple English, no trick questions").

Then one part changes each time — the task slot: "This week's topic: ____". Save the fixed parts once; fill the slot forever.
blocks.goDeeper: This is the same idea that powers custom AI "assistants" — a fixed set of instructions, often called a system prompt. You're just writing yours in plain words. No coding, no settings. A saved prompt in your Toolkit is your mini-assistant.

blocks.prompt: Assemble a reusable quiz-maker prompt — the fixed setup first, the part that changes last.

items.text: Role: "You are a quiz-maker for my class."
Rules: "Always 5 MCQs, one mark each, with an answer key, in simple English."
Task slot: "This week's topic: ____ (I'll fill this in each time)."

blocks.question: How clear are you on what makes a prompt reusable — write once, reuse forever?
